vendor_name: Foundry Technologies, Inc. (dba Mithril, mithril.ai; formerly Foundry)
identification: IDENTIFICATION (confidence: medium-high, proceeding): 'Mithril' on Tavus's sub-processor list is identified as Mithril, the AI omnicloud GPU-compute platform at mithril.ai, operated by Foundry Technologies, Inc. (Palo Alto, CA; formerly branded 'Foundry', rebranded to Mithril per the vendor's own blog https://mithril.ai/blog/foundry-is-now-mithril). Basis: (1) categorical fit — Tavus's sub-processor list is heavy on GPU/inference infrastructure (Cerebrium, Fal, Cerebras, Groq per config/scope.yaml), and mithril.ai is exactly that: an 'AI omnicloud' that provisions multi-cloud NVIDIA GPU capacity for training and inference (customers incl. Cursor, LG AI Research, Arc Institute); (2) mithril.ai operates as a data processor for customers — it publishes a Data Processing Agreement at https://docs.mithril.ai/security-and-trust/legal/data-processing-agreement and a security-and-trust docs section, which only makes sense for a hosted processing service; (3) the alternative candidates are implausible: Mithril Security (mithrilsecurity.io) is a small Paris-based confidential-computing TOOLING company acquired by H Company in June 2024 — it sells enclave deployment software, not a hosted processing service a US video-AI company would subprocess to; a Korean 'Mithril' surfaced in search is a GPU-manufacturing hardware startup, not a service provider. CAVEAT reducing confidence from high: https://www.tavus.io/authorized-subprocessors could not be fetched this session (egress proxy blocks www.tavus.io, and web.archive.org is unreachable), and no search snippet exposed how Tavus's page actually describes the 'Mithril' entry — so the identification rests on the candidate space, not on Tavus's own wording. Also, no public statement linking Tavus and mithril.ai was found (Mithril's published customer names don't include Tavus; sub-processor relationships are routinely unpublicized, so this is weak absence-of-evidence). HUMAN MUST CONFIRM against the live tavus.io/authorized-subprocessors page (or the Tavus vendor register / Vanta) that the listed Mithril is mithril.ai / Foundry Technologies, Inc. before this column is submitted. Mithril is NOT in config/scope.yaml (which reflects the list effective 2026-04-27), so it appears to be a post-April-2026 addition to Tavus's list — consistent with a new GPU-compute vendor.
research_caveat: IMPORTANT: every Mithril-owned host (mithril.ai, docs.mithril.ai) returned an egress-proxy CONNECT 403 to both WebFetch and curl this session, and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment — no Mithril page could be fetched directly. Every sourced value below comes from Mithril's OWN pages (mithril.ai / docs.mithril.ai) as reflected in web-search result excerpts that named those pages as the source. Per researcher hard rules ('confidence: high requires a URL you actually fetched'), confidence is capped at 'low' everywhere. Third-party company profiles (Crunchbase, CB Insights, PitchBook, ZoomInfo, RocketReach) were NOT used as sources for any field value; where they were the only place a datum appeared (e.g. the 555 Bryant St address), the field is 'Not known' and the datum is mentioned in notes as unverified. Key vendor pages that exist but could not be read and very likely answer the open questions: https://docs.mithril.ai/security-and-trust/mithrils-approach-to-security (mentions a 'Trust Center' with the complete list of security measures), https://docs.mithril.ai/security-and-trust/legal/data-processing-agreement, https://docs.mithril.ai/security-and-trust/reporting-security-concerns, and the Privacy/Terms/Legal pages linked from mithril.ai's footer. The verifier pass should re-fetch each source_url from an unrestricted network before any value is promoted.

open_questions_for_vendor: Please confirm your full legal entity name, legal form and state of incorporation (we believe 'Foundry Technologies, Inc.', dba Mithril) and the registered address to be used for GDPR purposes (third-party profiles show 555 Bryant Street, Suite 123, Palo Alto, CA 94301 — please confirm or correct in writing).
Has Foundry Technologies, Inc. designated a representative in the Union under Article 27 GDPR? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address; if no, please confirm in writing.

Have you formally designated a Data Protection Officer? If yes, please provide the DPO's name and telephone number and/or email; if no, please provide the email address entitled to respond to data-protection-related requests (your docs reference a security-reporting email we could not read).
Which TLS version is enforced (minimum and preferred) for data in transit to/from the Mithril platform (console, compute API, and data paths to provisioned GPU instances)?
Which encryption-at-rest standard (algorithm and key length, e.g. AES-256) applies to customer data stored on or via the Mithril platform, and does the same standard cover backups?

Who generates and manages the encryption keys for customer data at rest — Mithril-managed keys (customer-specific or shared), the underlying cloud/datacenter provider, or is a customer-managed key (CMEK/BYOK) option available?

Can personal data processed on your platform be anonymized and/or pseudonymized by Mithril on the customer's instruction, or is that outside your role as a compute/IaaS provider (in which case please confirm 'not applicable' in writing)?

Please provide your current SOC 2 Type II report (your security page states SOC 2 Type II certification in availability, security, and confidentiality) via your Trust Center or directly to Tavus, so it can be placed on file in Vanta as audit evidence for row 1.4.2, and confirm any other certifications you hold (e.g. ISO 27001) — your page attributes ISO 27001 only to the datacenters you use.

For your EU compute regions (eu-north1, eu-central1, eu-west1 via Nebius): does selecting an EU region keep all customer personal data — including control-plane metadata, logs, and support access — within the EU, and please provide your current sub-processor list (Nebius and any other infrastructure providers) with locations.

Please confirm in writing the categories of Tavus data your platform touches (e.g. video/audio frames or model inputs during GPU inference vs. account metadata only) so the processing-operations description (row 1.1.3) can be drafted accurately.
